shifts.summary: The first shift was overall moderate in difficulty. Candidates reported attempting between 72 and 80 questions successfully. Reasoning was generally easy with 17–24 good attempts, while General Awareness showed a mixed difficulty and 15–17 good attempts. Quantitative section difficulty varied, with 14–22 good attempts. English difficulty ranged from easy to moderate with 17 good attempts.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Reasoning was the longest part, many statement‑based items. Candidates felt attempts were low.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GA content included current affairs up to 2023 and a few recent items. Scope was limited but questions were straightforward for some.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Math featured advanced problems and some lengthy items, causing time pressure.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English had many passage‑based items and a focus on direct/indirect speech and voice transformation.

shifts.summary: The shift 2 paper was reported overall as moderate in difficulty. Candidates said reasoning was generally easy to moderate, while GA and Quant were moderate and English ranged from easy to moderate. Good attempts varied, with overall attempts reported between 75 and 99. Time pressure was noted in English passages and the math section due to a sectional timer. Some candidates found certain reasoning matrix questions tougher.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude

sections.name: English Comprehension

shifts.summary: Candidates reported the paper overall as moderate in difficulty. Timing was a common issue, especially in reasoning and English. Good attempts varied widely, from 62 to 88 questions across reports. Quantitative section ranged from easy to moderate, while English was generally moderate.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Madhuvan noted easy but time‑taking, about 15 min per section. STH‑1 reported moderate‑to‑difficult level with 18‑22 good attempts. Student Saviour first mentioned timing as main issue with some math in reasoning. Student Saviour second said reasoning was excellent with only 1‑2 unsolved.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: Madhuvan listed two history, two current affairs and two constitution questions and called the section moderate. STH‑1 described it as moderate to difficult with 15‑18 good attempts. Student Saviour first said DI was average and advanced DI rare. Student Saviour second found GK easy with many 50‑50 questions.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Madhuvan called math easy but time‑taking, with 16 questions attempted. STH‑1 found it difficult with 14‑17 good attempts. Student Saviour first said most questions were circles, easy to moderate overall. Student Saviour second reported moderate difficulty with DI hard and other questions easy.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: Madhuvan described English as moderate with direct‑indirect and word‑relation items. STH‑1 reported moderate difficulty with 20‑22 good attempts. Student Saviour first said English was easy with AI‑style passages and 2‑3 good attempts. Student Saviour second noted moderate level with cloze and idioms, 23 good attempts.

observations: Timing problems were reported in reasoning and English sections.
Overall difficulty settled around moderate across most reports.
Good attempts varied widely, indicating differing candidate preparation levels.
Quantitative section showed the widest spread of difficulty labels.
disagreements: Reasoning difficulty split between moderate (2 reports) and moderate to difficult (1 report).
Quant difficulty ranged from easy to difficult across reports.
English difficulty was reported as easy by one report and moderate by others.

intro: On 12 October 2026, the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam was reported as moderate in difficulty across all three shifts. Candidates indicated unofficial good‑attempt ranges of 62–88, 72–80, and 75–99 questions overall, depending on the shift. Section‑wise, reasoning and English were generally easy to moderate, while General Awareness and Quantitative sections varied between easy and moderate. All figures are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level of the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 12 October 2026?
faqs.a: All three shifts on 12 October 2026 were reported as moderate in difficulty by the majority of candidates.

faqs.q: How many questions did candidates report attempting successfully on 12 October 2026?
faqs.a: Candidates gave unofficial good‑attempt ranges of 62–88, 72–80, and 75–99 questions overall across the three shifts on that date.

faqs.q: Which sections were considered easy or moderate on 12 October 2026?
faqs.a: Reasoning and English were generally described as easy to moderate, while General Awareness and Quantitative sections showed mixed difficulty, ranging from easy to moderate across the shifts.

faqs.q: Was time pressure reported as an issue on 12 October 2026?
faqs.a: Yes, candidates noted time pressure especially in the English passages and the mathematics sections, with some also mentioning timing challenges in reasoning.

faqs.q: Are the reported figures for 12 October 2026 official?
faqs.a: No, the figures are unofficial; SSC normalises scores across shifts, and the numbers provided reflect candidate reports rather than official statistics.
